title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
units.literal: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
units.idiomatic: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

units.zh: 惠帝乃止。
units.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

units.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
units.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
units.idiomatic: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

units.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
units.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

units.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
units.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
units.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

units.zh: 由是奇之。
units.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
units.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

units.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
units.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
units.idiomatic: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

units.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
units.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
units.idiomatic: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

units.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
units.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
units.idiomatic: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

units.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
units.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
units.idiomatic: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

units.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
units.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
units.idiomatic: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

units.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
units.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.
units.idiomatic: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.

units.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
units.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.
units.idiomatic: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.

units.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
units.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
units.idiomatic: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

units.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
units.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.
units.idiomatic: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.

units.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
units.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

units.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
units.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
units.idiomatic: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

units.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
units.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.
units.idiomatic: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.

units.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
units.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.
units.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.

units.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
units.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.
units.idiomatic: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.

units.zh: 其高皇、太皇、處士君等，並為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
units.literal: The High Emperor, Grand Emperor, Recluse Lord, and others were all kin seniors—not in the zhao-mu combined-feasting array.
units.idiomatic: The High Emperor, Grand Emperor, Recluse Lord, and others were all kin seniors—not in the zhao-mu combined-feasting array.

units.zh: 晉宣創業，武帝受命，亦即以宣帝為太祖。
units.literal: Jin Xuan founded the enterprise and Emperor Wu received the mandate; he too took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor.
units.idiomatic: Jin Xuan founded the enterprise and Emperor Wu received the mandate; he too took Emperor Xuan as Grand Ancestor.

units.zh: 其征西、潁川等四府君，亦為屬尊，不在昭穆合食之列。
units.literal: The Western Campaign General, Yingchuan, and the other four lords were also kin seniors—not in the zhao-mu combined-feasting array.
units.idiomatic: The Western Campaign General, Yingchuan, and the other four lords were also kin seniors—not in the zhao-mu combined-feasting array.

title.raw: 《五宗世家》 House of the Five Clans

units.zh: 景帝賜非將軍印，擊吳。
units.literal: Emperor Jing granted Fei a general's seal and sent him to attack Wu.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Jing bestowed upon Fei a general's seal and dispatched him to fight against Wu.

units.zh: 吳已破，二歲，徙為江都王，治吳故國，以軍功賜天子旌旗。
units.literal: After Wu was defeated, two years later he was moved to become King of Jiangdu, ruling the former Wu territory. For his military achievements, he was granted the emperor's banners.
units.idiomatic: After Wu was crushed, two years passed before Fei was transferred to become King of Jiangdu, governing the former territory of Wu. In recognition of his military valor, he was awarded the imperial banners.

units.zh: 元光五年，匈奴大入漢為賊，非上書願擊匈奴，上不許。
units.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanguang, the Xiongnu invaded Han territory on a large scale. Fei petitioned to attack the Xiongnu, but the emperor would not allow it.
units.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yuanguang era, the Xiongnu launched a major incursion into Han territory, raiding and plundering. Fei submitted a memorial requesting permission to strike against them, but the emperor refused.

units.zh: 非好氣力，治宮觀，招四方豪桀，驕奢甚。
units.literal: Fei was fond of physical strength and built palaces and towers. He attracted bold heroes from all directions and lived in great extravagance.
units.idiomatic: Fei delighted in feats of strength, built lavish palaces and towers, and gathered bold and daring men from every quarter. His arrogance and extravagance knew no bounds.

units.zh: 淮南、衡山謀反時，建頗聞其謀。
units.literal: During the Huainan and Hengshan rebellion, Jian had heard rumors of their plot.
units.idiomatic: When the kings of Huainan and Hengshan were plotting rebellion, Jian had caught wind of their conspiracy.

units.zh: 自以為國近淮南，恐一日發，為所并，即陰作兵器，而時佩其父所賜將軍印，載天子旗以出。
units.literal: Since his kingdom bordered Huainan, he feared that if rebellion broke out he would be annexed. So he secretly manufactured weapons while always wearing his father's general's seal and going out with the emperor's banners.
units.idiomatic: Believing his kingdom lay dangerously close to Huainan, he feared that should the revolt erupt, he might be swallowed up. He therefore had weapons forged in secret, and whenever he ventured out he wore the general's seal his father had received and displayed the imperial banners.

units.zh: 易王死未葬，建有所說易王寵美人淖姬，夜使人迎與姦服舍中。
units.literal: Before King Yi was even buried, Jian took a fancy to King Yi's favored beauty Nao Ji and sent men at night to bring her to his chambers for illicit relations.
units.idiomatic: Before King Yi had even been laid to rest, Jian became enamored of the late king's favored consort, Lady Nao. Under cover of night he sent men to bring her to his quarters, where he took her as his own.

units.zh: 事既聞，漢公卿請捕治建。
units.literal: When this became known, Han nobles requested Jian's arrest and trial.
units.idiomatic: When these affairs came to light, the ministers and nobles of the Han court petitioned for Jian's arrest and prosecution.

units.zh: 天子不忍，使大臣即訊王。
units.literal: The Son of Heaven spared him and sent ministers to interrogate the king.
units.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven could not bear to act so harshly and instead sent senior ministers to interrogate the king in person.

units.zh: 王服所犯，遂自殺。
units.literal: The king admitted his crimes and committed suicide.
units.idiomatic: The king confessed to his offenses and then took his own life.

units.zh: 為郎者頃之與後宮亂，端禽滅之，及殺其子母。
units.literal: This attendant soon committed adultery with the women of the rear palace. Duan captured and executed him, along with his mother and children.
units.idiomatic: Before long, this attendant carried on illicit affairs with the women of the inner palace. Duan seized and put him to death, and killed his mother and children as well.

units.zh: 數犯上法，漢公卿數請誅端，天子為兄弟之故不忍，而端所為滋甚。
units.literal: He repeatedly violated the laws of the court. Han's nobles and ministers repeatedly requested his execution, but the emperor spared him for the sake of brotherhood. Yet Duan's offenses grew worse.
units.idiomatic: He transgressed the imperial statutes time and again. The ministers and nobles of the Han court repeatedly petitioned for his execution, but the Son of Heaven, for the bond of brotherhood, could not bring himself to act. Meanwhile, Duan's outrages only grew worse.

units.zh: 有司再請削其國，去太半。
units.literal: The officials twice requested that his kingdom be reduced, removing more than half.
units.idiomatic: The responsible officials twice petitioned to have his kingdom reduced, and more than half its territory was stripped away.

units.zh: 王者當日聽音樂聲色。」
units.literal: As king, one should daily listen to music and enjoy beauty.'
units.idiomatic: A king ought to spend his days enjoying music and the pleasures of the senses."

units.zh: 趙王亦非之，曰：「中山王徒日淫，不佐天子拊循百姓，何以稱為藩臣！」
units.literal: The King of Zhao also quarreled with him, saying: 'The King of Zhongshan merely indulges in debauchery daily, does not assist the Son of Heaven in comforting and guiding the people. How can he be called a vassal minister!'
units.idiomatic: The King of Zhao countered: "The King of Zhongshan does nothing but wallow in excess day after day. He does not assist the Son of Heaven in nurturing and guiding the people. How can he claim to be a worthy vassal?"

units.zh: 立四十二年卒，子哀王昌立。
units.literal: He reigned for forty-two years and died. His son, King Ai Chang, succeeded him.
units.idiomatic: After forty-two years on the throne he died, and his son, King Ai, whose name was Chang, succeeded him.

units.zh: 及吏治淮南之事，辭出之。
units.literal: When officials investigated the Huainan affair, the evidence implicated him.
units.idiomatic: When officials investigated the Huainan affair, the confessions that emerged implicated him.

units.zh: 寄於上最親，意傷之，發病而死，不敢置後，於是上（問）［聞］。
units.literal: Ji was most beloved by the emperor, who was grieved by this. Ji fell ill and died, not daring to appoint an heir. Thus, the emperor heard of it.
units.idiomatic: Ji had been the emperor's most beloved brother, and the affair weighed heavily upon him. He fell ill with grief and died, not having dared to designate an heir. Only then did the emperor learn what had happened.

units.zh: 寄有長子者名賢，母無寵；
units.literal: Ji had an eldest son named Xian whose mother had no favor.
units.idiomatic: Ji's eldest son was named Xian, but his mother had never enjoyed imperial favor;

units.zh: 漢使者視憲王喪，棁自言憲王病時，王后、太子不侍，及薨，六日出舍，太子勃私姦，飲酒，博戲，擊筑，與女子載馳，環城過市，入牢視囚。
units.literal: Han envoys inspecting King Xian's funeral, Tiao personally stated that during King Xian's illness, the queen and crown prince did not attend. When he died, they left the residence after six days. Crown Prince Bo privately committed adultery, drank wine, gambled, played zither, raced chariots with women, circled the city through the markets, and entered prisons to inspect prisoners.
units.idiomatic: When Han envoys arrived to oversee King Xian's funeral, Tiao came forward and personally testified that during the king's illness, neither the queen nor the crown prince had attended him. After the king's death, they had left their mourning quarters within six days. He further reported that Crown Prince Bo had conducted illicit affairs, drunk wine, gambled, and played the bamboo zither. He had raced in carriages with women through the streets, ridden around the city walls and through the markets, and entered the prison to inspect the inmates.

units.zh: 天子遣大行騫驗王后及問王勃，請逮勃所與姦諸證左，王又匿之。
units.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Grand Herald Qian to investigate the queen and interrogate King Bo, requesting to arrest Bo's accomplices in adultery and witnesses. The king hid them.
units.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven dispatched the Grand Herald, Qian, to investigate the queen and interrogate King Bo. He requested the arrest of all accomplices and witnesses to Bo's illicit activities, but the king concealed them.

units.zh: 吏求捕勃大急，使人致擊笞掠，擅出漢所疑囚者。
units.literal: When officials urgently sought to apprehend Bo, he had men inflict beatings and floggings, and arbitrarily released prisoners whom the Han court held under suspicion.
units.idiomatic: When the officials pressed urgently to apprehend Bo, he had his men resort to beatings and floggings, and he took it upon himself to release prisoners whom the Han court had placed under suspicion.

units.zh: 勃王數月，遷于房陵，國絕。
units.literal: Bo had been king for several months when he was moved to Fangling. The kingdom was extinguished.
units.idiomatic: Bo had reigned as king for only a few months before he was removed to Fangling, and the kingdom came to an end.

units.zh: 月餘，天子為最親，乃詔有司曰：「常山憲王蚤夭，后妾不和，適孽誣爭，陷于不義以滅國，朕甚閔焉。
units.literal: More than a month later, considering that he was most beloved, the emperor instructed the officials: 'King Xian of Changshan died young. His queen and consorts were not harmonious. Legitimate and illegitimate sons slandered and contended, falling into unrighteousness and extinguishing the kingdom. I greatly pity this.
units.idiomatic: A little more than a month later, mindful that Changshan had been ruled by his closest kin, the Son of Heaven issued an edict to his ministers: "King Xian of Changshan died before his time. His queen and consorts were at odds, and legitimate and illegitimate sons slandered one another and quarreled until they fell into disgrace and the kingdom was extinguished. We are deeply grieved by this.

units.zh: 其封憲王子平三萬戶，為真定王；
units.literal: Let King Xian's son Ping be enfeoffed with thirty thousand households as King of Zhending;
units.idiomatic: Enfeoff King Xian's son Ping as King of Zhending, with thirty thousand households;

units.zh: 太史公曰：高祖時諸侯皆賦，得自除內史以下，漢獨為置丞相，黃金印。
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: In Gaozu's time the feudal lords all collected their own taxes and were able to appoint their own officials from the rank of interior minister downward. Only the Han court appointed chancellors for them, with golden seals.
units.idiomatic: The Grand Historian remarks: In the time of Emperor Gaozu, the feudal lords all collected their own taxes and were permitted to appoint their own officials from the rank of Interior Minister downward. Only the chancellors were appointed by the Han court, and they bore golden seals.

units.zh: 諸侯自除御史、廷尉正、博士，擬於天子。
units.literal: The feudal lords appointed their own censors, directors of convicts at the Court of Justice, and erudites, rivaling the Son of Heaven.
units.idiomatic: The feudal lords appointed their own censors, chief justices, and erudites, rivaling the Son of Heaven in their establishments.

units.zh: 自吳楚反後，五宗王世，漢為置二千石，去「丞相」曰「相」，銀印。
units.literal: After the Wu and Chu rebellion, the five clans of kings generation after generation, Han appointed officials of two thousand shi for them, removed 'chancellor' and called it 'prime minister', silver seal.
units.idiomatic: After the rebellion of Wu and Chu, through the successive generations of the five royal lineages, the Han court appointed officials of two-thousand-shi rank in every kingdom, replaced the title of "chancellor" with the lesser designation of "administrator," and issued silver seals in place of gold.

title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第五十三 王神念 羊侃 羊鴉仁 Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren

units.zh: 神念少善騎射，及老不衰。
units.literal: Shennian from youth was skilled in mounted archery, and even when old he did not decline.
units.idiomatic: Shennian had been skilled in horsemanship and archery since youth, and even in old age he had not lost his edge.

units.zh: 嘗于武帝前手執二刀楯，左右交度，馭馬往來，冠絕群伍。
units.literal: Once before Emperor Wu he held two sabers and shields in his hands, crossing them left and right, driving his horse back and forth, surpassing all the ranks.
units.idiomatic: Once before Emperor Wu he took two sabers and shields in hand, crossing them left and right as he drove his horse to and fro—a feat unmatched in the whole company.

units.zh: 時復有楊華者，能作驚軍騎，亦一時妙捷，帝深賞之。
units.literal: At the same time there was also Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry maneuvers; he too was a marvel of agility for the age, and the Emperor deeply admired him.
units.idiomatic: At the same time there was Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry feats—another marvel of the day whom the Emperor greatly admired.

units.zh: 華本名白花，武都仇池人。
units.literal: Hua's original name was Bai Hua; he was a man of Chouchi in Wudu.
units.idiomatic: Hua had originally been named Bai Hua and came from Chouchi in Wudu.

title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二: 高祖下
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二: 高祖下 Volume 2: Emperor Wu 2

units.zh: [12]辛卯，詔車騎將軍、司空侯瑱總督水步眾軍以遏齊寇。
units.literal: [12] On xinmao day an edict ordered Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Works Hou Tian to take overall command of the water and land combined armies to check the Qi invaders.
units.idiomatic: [12] On xinmao day an edict placed Hou Tian, grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of works, in overall command of naval and land forces to block the Qi invasion.

units.zh: 三月甲午，詔曰：「罰不及嗣，自古通典，罪疑惟輕，布在方策。
units.literal: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict said: "Punishment does not reach the sons—this is an ancient universal canon; when guilt is doubtful, lean toward leniency—it is set forth in the statutes.
units.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu day, an edict declared: "Punishment does not fall on heirs—so the ancients taught; when guilt is in doubt, favor mercy—so the law books say.

units.zh: 沈泰反覆無行，遐邇所知，昔有微功，仍荷朝寄，剖符名郡，推轂累藩，漢口班師，還居方岳，良田有逾於四百，食客不止於三千，富貴顯榮，政當如此。
units.literal: Shen Tai was fickle and without conduct, known far and near. In the past he had slight merit and still bore the court's trust; with divided tally he held a famed commandery, with chariot-shaft he was pushed up through many border posts. When the army withdrew from Hankou he returned to a territorial post. Good fields exceeded four hundred; retainers numbered no fewer than three thousand—wealth, honor, and glory ought indeed to be thus.
units.idiomatic: Shen Tai was treacherous and faithless, known throughout the realm. He had once done minor service and still held the court's trust; enfeoffed in a great commandery, promoted through many frontier posts. After the Hankou campaign he returned to provincial command. His estates ran to four hundred fields; his retainers to three thousand—such were the rewards of his rank.

units.zh: 若樂隨臨川王及節將立效者，悉皆聽許。」
units.literal: If any wish to follow the King of Linchuan and the commanders bearing staffs to render merit, all are permitted."
units.idiomatic: Those who wish to serve the King of Linchuan or other commanders in earning merit may do so."

units.zh: 乙卯，高祖幸後堂聽訟，還於橋上觀山水，賦詩示群臣。
units.literal: On yimao day the Founder visited the rear hall to hear lawsuits; returning, on the bridge he viewed mountains and waters and composed a poem to show the assembled ministers.
units.idiomatic: On yimao day the Founder heard cases in the rear hall; on his way back he paused on the bridge to take in the landscape and wrote a poem for his ministers.

units.zh: 是月，王琳立梁永嘉王蕭莊于郢州。
units.literal: That month Wang Lin installed Liang's Prince of Yongjia, Xiao Zhuang, at Yingzhou.
units.idiomatic: That month Wang Lin set up Xiao Zhuang, Prince of Yongjia of Liang, at Yingzhou.

units.zh: 夏四月甲子，輿駕親祠太廟。
units.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on jiazi, the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
units.idiomatic: On jiazi in the fourth month of summer, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

units.zh: 乙丑，江陰王薨，詔遣太宰弔祭，司空監護喪事，凶禮所須，隨由備辦。
units.literal: On yichou, the Prince of Jiangyin died; an edict sent the Grand Steward to offer condolences and sacrifices, had the Minister of Works supervise the funeral affairs, and ordered that whatever the mourning rites required be supplied according to need.
units.idiomatic: On yichou, the Prince of Jiangyin died. An edict sent the Grand Steward to offer condolences and sacrifices, placed the Minister of Works in charge of the funeral, and ordered that everything required for the mourning rites be supplied as needed.

units.zh: 以梁武林侯蕭諮息季卿嗣為江陰王。
units.literal: Xiao Zhi's son Jiqing, of the Liang Marquis of Wulin, was made to succeed as Prince of Jiangyin.
units.idiomatic: Jiqing, son of Xiao Zhi (Liang Marquis of Wulin), was made successor as Prince of Jiangyin.

units.zh: 景寅，輿駕幸石頭，餞司空侯瑱。
units.literal: On bingyin, the imperial carriage visited Shitou and held a farewell banquet for Hou Tian, Minister of Works.
units.idiomatic: On bingyin, the emperor visited Shitou and gave a farewell banquet for Hou Tian, the Minister of Works.

units.zh: 戊辰，重雲殿東鴟尾有紫煙屬天。
units.literal: On wuchen, from the eastern chiwei roof ornament of Chongyun Hall, purple smoke reached up to the sky.
units.idiomatic: On wuchen, purple smoke rose to the sky from the eastern chiwei roof ornament of Chongyun Hall.

units.zh: 癸丑，齊廣陵南城主張顯和、長史張僧那各率其所部入附。
units.literal: On guichou, Zhang Xianhe, commander of Qi's Southern Guangling city, and Zhang Sengna, the chief secretary, each led the troops under his command and came over in submission.
units.idiomatic: On guichou, Zhang Xianhe, commander of Qi's Southern Guangling city, and the chief secretary Zhang Sengna each led his command in submission.

units.zh: 辛酉，輿駕幸大莊嚴寺捨身。
units.literal: On xinyou, the imperial carriage visited Dazhuangyan Monastery and offered his body.
units.idiomatic: On xinyou, the emperor visited Dazhuangyan Monastery and performed the Buddhist rite of offering himself.

units.zh: 壬戌，群臣表請還宮。
units.literal: On renxu, the assembled ministers memorialized requesting that he return to the palace.
units.idiomatic: On renxu, the assembled ministers submitted a memorial asking him to return to the palace.

units.zh: 六月己巳，詔司空侯瑱、領軍將軍徐度率舟師為前軍，以討王琳。
units.literal: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Minister of Works Hou Tian and Palace Bulwark General Xu Du to lead the fleet as the vanguard army to attack Wang Lin.
units.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jisi day, an edict ordered Hou Tian, minister of works, and Xu Du, palace bulwark general, to lead the fleet as vanguard against Wang Lin.

units.zh: 秋七月戊戌，輿駕幸石頭，親送填等。
units.literal: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the imperial carriage went to Stone City and personally sent off Tian and the others.
units.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on wuxu day, the emperor went to Stone City and personally saw off Hou Tian and the commanders.

units.zh: 己亥，江州刺史周迪擒王琳將李孝欽、樊猛、余孝頃于工塘。
units.literal: On jihai day Jiangzhou Inspector Zhou Di captured Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoqing at Gongtang.
units.idiomatic: On jihai day Zhou Di, inspector of Jiangzhou, took Wang Lin's generals Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoqing at Gongtang.

units.zh: 八月景寅，以廣梁郡為陳留郡。
units.literal: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was made Chenliu commandery.
units.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yingyin day, Guangliang commandery was renamed Chenliu.

units.zh: 辛未，詔臨川王蒨西討，[13]以舟師五萬發自京師，輿駕幸冶城寺親送焉。
units.literal: On xinwei day an edict ordered the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign; [13] with a fleet of fifty thousand he set out from the capital, and the imperial carriage went to Ye City Monastery to see him off in person.
units.idiomatic: On xinwei day an edict sent the King of Linchuan, Qian, on the western campaign. [13] With fifty thousand sailors he sailed from the capital, and the emperor went in person to Ye City Monastery to see him off.

units.zh: 前開府儀同三司、南豫州刺史周文育，前鎮北將軍、南徐州刺史、新除開府儀同三司侯安都等於王琳所逃歸，自劾廷尉，即日引見，並宥之。
units.literal: Former Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and South Yuzhou Inspector Zhou Wenyü, and former General Who Pacifies the North, South Xuzhou Inspector, and newly appointed Grand Mentor with Staff Hou Andu, who had escaped from Wang Lin's custody, impeached themselves before the Court for Punishments; that same day they were received in audience and all were pardoned.
units.idiomatic: Zhou Wenyü, former grand mentor with staff and inspector of South Yuzhou, and Hou Andu, former general who pacifies the north, inspector of South Xuzhou, and newly made grand mentor with staff, who had escaped Wang Lin, presented themselves to the court of punishments to confess fault; that day they were received and pardoned.

units.zh: 戊寅，詔復文育等本官。
units.literal: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former offices.
units.idiomatic: On wuyin day an edict restored Wenyü and the others to their former posts.

units.zh: 壬午，追封皇子立為豫章王，諡曰獻；
units.literal: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;
units.idiomatic: On renwu day the Founder's son Li was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yuzhang, posthumous name Xian;

units.zh: 權為長沙王，諡曰思；
units.literal: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;
units.idiomatic: Quan as King of Changsha, posthumous name Si;

units.zh: 長女為永世公主，諡曰懿。
units.literal: the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.
units.idiomatic: and the eldest daughter as Princess of Eternal Generations, posthumous name Yi.

units.zh: 謝哲反命，王琳請還鎮湘川，詔追眾軍緩其伐。
units.literal: Xie Zhe returned with a contrary mandate. Wang Lin asked to return and hold Xiang River; an edict recalled the armies and suspended the campaign.
units.idiomatic: Xie Zhe returned from his mission. Wang Lin asked to go back and hold the Xiang River region; an edict recalled the armies and halted the offensive.

units.zh: 冬十月庚午，遣鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司周文育都督眾軍出豫章，討余孝勱。
units.literal: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Pacifying South General and Grand Mentor with Staff Zhou Wenyü was sent as commander-in-chief of the armies to march out of Yuzhang to attack Yu Xiaoqing.
units.idiomatic: In the tenth month, on gengwu day, Zhou Wenyü, pacifying south general and grand mentor with staff, was sent from Yuzhang at the head of the armies against Yu Xiaoqing.

units.zh: 乙亥，輿駕幸莊嚴寺，發金光明經題。
units.literal: On yihai day the imperial carriage visited Zhuangyan Monastery and opened the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.
units.idiomatic: On yihai day the emperor went to Zhuangyan Monastery to inaugurate the lecture on the Sutra of Golden Light.

units.zh: 丁酉，以仁威將軍、高州刺史黃法𣰋為開府儀同三司，[14]進號鎮南將軍。
units.literal: On dingyou day the Benevolent and Martial General and Gaozhou Inspector Huang Fa Tu was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes [14] and promoted to General Who Guards the South.
units.idiomatic: On dingyou day Huang Fa Tu, benevolent and martial general and inspector of Gaozhou, was made grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes [14] and promoted to general who guards the south.

title.zh: 卷九十四 列傳第六十四 隱逸
title.raw: 卷九十四 列傳第六十四 隱逸 Volume 94 Biographies 64: Hermits and Recluses

units.zh: 郁，魏徵士原之曾孫，少有原風，敕身謹潔，口不妄說，耳不妄聽，端拱恂恂，舉動有禮。
units.literal: Yu was great-grandson of Wei recluse Bing Yuan; in youth he had Yuan's air, ordering the self chaste and clean, mouth not speaking rashly, ears not listening rashly, sitting upright and earnest, every motion with ritual.
units.idiomatic: Bing Yu was Bing Yuan's heir: silent, careful, every gesture correct.

units.zh: 咸康中，成帝博求異行之士，鮞、鬱並被公卿薦舉，於是依績及翟湯等例，以博士徵之。
units.literal: In Xiankang, Emperor Cheng broadly sought men of unusual conduct; Jun and Yu were together recommended by dukes and ministers; thereupon according to the precedent of Ji and Zhai Tang and others they were summoned as erudites.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng sought odd talents; both were nominated like Han Ji and Zhai Tang.

units.zh: 鬱辭以疾，鮞隨使者到京師，自陳年老，不拜。
units.literal: Yu declined on grounds of illness; Jun followed the envoy to the capital, personally declaring old age and not taking office.
units.idiomatic: Yu pleaded sick; Liu Jun went to the capital, declared himself too old, and refused the cap.

units.zh: 寶本以為惠，而更煩之，益愧歎焉。
units.literal: Bao had thought it a kindness, yet it only troubled him the more; he increased in shame and admiration.
units.idiomatic: Gan Bao meant a favor yet felt only shame and deeper respect.

units.zh: 咸康中，征西大將軍庾亮上疏薦之，成帝徵為國子博士，湯不起。
units.literal: In Xiankang, General Who Stabilizes the West Yu Liang submitted a memorial recommending him; Emperor Cheng summoned him as national university erudite; Tang did not rise.
units.idiomatic: Yu Liang recommended him; Emperor Cheng named him national erudite; he stayed home.

units.zh: 建元初，安西將軍庾翼北征石季龍，大發僮客以充戎役，敕有司特蠲湯所調。
units.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, General Who Pacifies the West Yu Yi on northern campaign against Shi Hu greatly conscripted retainers and guests to fill military service, ordering the offices specially to remit Tang's levy.
units.idiomatic: Yu Yi's levy on retainers skipped Zhai Tang by edict.

title.zh: 卷二十四 志第十四 職官
title.raw: 卷二十四 志第十四 職官 Volume 24 Treatises 14: Government Service

units.zh: 至魏，別為一台，位次御史中丞，掌授節、銅武符、竹使符。
units.literal: By Wei it became a separate bureau ranking below the assistant director, managing issuance of credentials, bronze martial tallies, and bamboo mission tallies.
units.idiomatic: Wei gave tallies its own desk below the assistant director for seals and tokens.

units.zh: 及泰始九年，武帝省並蘭台，置符節御史掌其事焉。
units.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi Emperor Wu merged it into the Orchid Terrace and established tally censors to manage those affairs.
units.idiomatic: 273 CE folded tally duty back into the terrace.

units.zh: 司隸校尉，案漢武初置十三州，刺史各一人，又置司隸校尉，察三輔、三河、弘農七郡，曆漢東京及魏晉，其官不替。
units.literal: Metropolitan Commandant—in tradition Emperor Wu of Han first established thirteen provinces with one inspector each; he also established the Metropolitan Commandant to inspect the Three Adjuncts, the Three Rivers, and Hongnong—seven commanderies. Through Eastern Han and Wei-Jin the office continued unchanged.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han first established thirteen provinces with one inspector each, and also established the Metropolitan Commandant to inspect the seven commanderies of the Three Adjuncts, the Three Rivers, and Hongnong; the office continued unchanged through Eastern Han, Wei, and Jin.

units.zh: 魏置僕射，掌大拜授及百官班次，統謁者十人。
units.literal: Wei established chief steward directing grand investitures and court seating order, supervising ten ushers.
units.idiomatic: Wei's chief steward staged audiences and lineups with ten ushers.

units.zh: 及武帝省僕射，以謁者並蘭台。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu cut chief steward, ushers merged into the Orchid Terrace.
units.idiomatic: Wudi merged ushers into the terrace.

units.zh: 江左復置僕射，後又省。
units.literal: East of the Yangzi chief steward was restored; later cut again.
units.idiomatic: South of the river restored then dropped the steward.

units.zh: 漢東京省都水，置河堤謁者，魏因之。
units.literal: Eastern Han cut unified water office and placed river-dike ushers; Wei continued.
units.idiomatic: Later Han switched to dike ushers; Wei kept them.

units.zh: 及武帝省水衡，置都水使者一人，以河堤謁者為都水官屬。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu cut the superintendent of waters he established one water superintendent envoy, making river-dike ushers subordinates of water offices.
units.idiomatic: Wudi replaced the old water ministry with one envoy over dike officers.

units.zh: 及江左，省河堤謁者，置謁者六人。
units.literal: East of the Yangzi river-dike ushers were cut and six ushers were placed.
units.idiomatic: South of the river swapped dike ushers for six general ushers.

title.zh: 新唐書卷二十七上 志第十七上 曆三上

units.zh: 而淳風冬至常在斗十三度，豈當時知不及牽牛五度，而不知過建星八度耶？
units.literal: Yet Chunfeng's winter solstice constantly stood at thirteen degrees in Dipper—could he then have known it fell five degrees short of Ox but not known it passed eight degrees beyond Jian?
units.idiomatic: Yet Chunfeng placed the winter solstice constantly at thirteen degrees in the Dipper—could he have known it fell five degrees short of Ox yet not known it overshot Jian by eight degrees?

units.zh: 晉武帝太始三年丁亥歲冬至，日當在斗十六度。
units.literal: In Taishi year 3 of Emperor Wu of Jin, the Dinghai year's winter solstice, the sun ought to have been at sixteen degrees in Dipper.
units.idiomatic: At the Dinghai winter solstice in Jin Emperor Wu's Taishi year 3, the sun should have stood at sixteen degrees in the Dipper.

units.zh: 晉用魏景初曆，其冬至亦在斗二十一度少。
units.literal: Jin used Wei's Jingchu calendar; its winter solstice also stood at a little more than twenty-one degrees in Dipper.
units.idiomatic: Jin used Wei's Jingchu calendar, whose winter solstice also fell at just over twenty-one degrees in the Dipper.

title.zh: 卷十三 志第三 禮樂三
title.raw: 卷十三 志第三 禮樂三 Volume 13 Treatises 3: Rites and Music 3

units.zh: 議者又言：「廟室有定數，而無後之主當置別廟。」
units.literal: Deliberators also said: "Temple chambers have fixed numbers; lords without heirs should be placed in separate temples."
units.idiomatic: Critics also said: "Temple chambers have fixed numbers; lords without heirs need separate temples."

units.zh: 禮官曰：「晉武帝時，景、文同廟，廟雖六代，其實七主。
units.literal: Ritual officers said: "Under Jin Emperor Wu, Jing and Wen shared a temple—though six generations in name, actually seven lords.
units.idiomatic: Ritual officers said: "Under Jin Emperor Wu, Jing and Wen shared a temple—six generations in name, seven lords in fact.

units.zh: 至元帝、明帝，廟皆十室，故賀循曰：『廟以容主為限，而無常數也。』」
units.literal: Under Yuan and Ming, temples all had ten chambers; hence He Xun said: 'Temples are limited by capacity for tablets, not by fixed number.'
units.idiomatic: Under Yuan and Ming, temples had ten chambers; He Xun said: 'Temples are limited by capacity for tablets, not by fixed number.'"

title.zh: 卷四 帝紀第四 孝惠帝
title.raw: 卷四 帝紀第四 孝惠帝 Volume 4 Annals 4: Emperor Hui

units.zh: 戊戌，大赦，復皇后羊氏及皇太子覃。
units.literal: On the wuxu day a general amnesty restored Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan.
units.idiomatic: Empress Yang and Crown Prince Tan were restored on wuxu under a general amnesty.

units.zh: 己亥，司徒王戎、東海王越、高密王簡、平昌公模、吳王晏、豫章王熾、襄陽王範、右僕射荀藩等奉帝北征。
units.literal: On the jihai day Minister of Education Wang Rong, Prince Yue of Donghai, Prince Jian of Gaomi, Duke Mo of Pingchang, Prince Yan of Wu, Prince Chi of Yuzhang, Prince Fan of Xiangyang, and Right Vice Director Xun Fan and others escorted the emperor on a northern expedition.
units.idiomatic: On jihai Wang Rong, Prince Yue, Prince Jian, Sima Mo, Prince Yan, Prince Chi, Prince Fan, and Xun Fan convoyed the emperor north.

units.zh: 至安陽，眾十餘萬，穎遣其將石超距戰。
units.literal: When they reached Anyang the host exceeded one hundred thousand; Ying dispatched his general Shi Chao to resist in battle.
units.idiomatic: The army swelled past a hundred thousand at Anyang, where Prince Ying sent Shi Chao to bar the road.

title.zh: 卷八十六 列傳第五十六 張軌
title.raw: 卷八十六 列傳第五十六 張軌 Volume 86 Biographies 56: Zhang Gui

units.zh: 秦王天挺聖德，神武應期。
units.literal: The Prince of Qin is heaven-endowed with sagely virtue, divine in arms and fitted to the hour.’
units.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin bears heaven’s sagely virtue, a warlike spirit born for the moment.

units.zh: 世祖之孫，王今為長。
units.literal: He is a grandson of Emperor Shizu; you, Prince, are now the senior among us.
units.idiomatic: You are of Shizu’s line, and among the princes you now stand first.

units.zh: 凡我晉人，食土之類，龜筮克從，幽明同款。
units.literal: All of us people of Jin who live on this soil—tortoise-shell and milfoil approve, and the spirits of light and dark are of one mind.
units.idiomatic: Every Jin subject dwelling on this earth finds tortoise and milfoil in accord, and both realms of the unseen give their assent.

title.zh: 卷十四 志第四 地理上
title.raw: 卷十四 志第四 地理上 Volume 14 Treatises 4: Geography Part One

units.zh: 時逢稽浸，道接陵夷，平王東遷，星離豆剖，當塗馭宇，瓜分鼎立。
units.literal: Times encountered famine-floods; the Way met decline; King Ping moved east; stars scattered, beans split; the cart-track clan grasped the cosmos; melons divided, tripod stood apart.
units.idiomatic: Then came years of flood and dearth, the royal Way slid downhill, Pingwang fled east and the realm shattered like stars and pods, the Caos seized the chariot-reins, and the land was carved into three rival stoves.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝接千祀之餘，當八堯之禪，先王桑梓，罄宇來歸，斯固可得而言者矣。
units.literal: Shizu Emperor Wu took up the remainder after a thousand sacrifices, faced the abdication like the eight Yao transfers; the Former Kings' mulberry and catalpa— the whole realm came to return—this indeed can be spoken of.
units.idiomatic: Our martial founding emperor, Shizu, picked up the threads after a thousand years of sacrifice, stood in the moment of a mandate-shift worthy of Yao's age, and watched the old heartland—the mulberry-and-catalpa home of the kings—empty itself back into his hands; that much, at least, can be told aloud.

units.zh: 惠皇不虞，中州盡棄，永嘉南度，綸行建鄴，九分天下而有二焉。
units.literal: Emperor Hui met unexpected disaster; the central plain was wholly abandoned; Yongjia southward crossing, by edict-progress establishing Jiankang; of nine parts of all under heaven they had two.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui fell to calamity the Central Plain was lost; after the Yongjia flight south the court set its capital at Jianye by imperial decree, holding barely two shares of a realm once counted in ninths.

units.zh: 乾明元年，齊廢帝以湯爲使持節、領東夷校尉、遼東郡公、高麗王。
units.literal: In the first year of Qianming, the Deposed Emperor of Qi made Tang Holder of the Staff, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Goguryeo.
units.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianming the Deposed Emperor of Qi invested Tang as holder of the staff of authority, colonel of the Eastern Yi, duke of Liaodong commandery, and king of Goguryeo.

units.zh: 周建德六年，湯遣使至周，武帝以湯爲上開府儀同大將軍、遼東郡公、遼東王。
units.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande under Zhou, Tang sent envoys to Zhou; Emperor Wu of Zhou made Tang Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General, Duke of Liaodong commandery, and King of Liaodong.
units.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande under Zhou, Tang sent envoys to Zhou, and Emperor Wu of Zhou invested him as Senior Opening-the-Fu Grand General, Duke of Liaodong, and King of Liaodong.

units.zh: 隋文帝受禪，湯遣使詣闕，進授大將軍，改封高麗王。
units.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, Tang sent envoys to the court; he was promoted to Grand General and re-invested as King of Goguryeo.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Tang sent envoys to court, was promoted to Grand General, and was re-invested as King of Goguryeo.

units.zh: 夫百王之御士也，莫不資伏羣才，以隆治道。
units.literal: Of the hundred kings' governing of scholars, none did not rely on and submit to the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.
units.idiomatic: In governing scholars, none of the hundred kings failed to rely on the host of talents to elevate the governing Way.

units.zh: 故周文以多士克寧，漢武以得賢為盛。
units.literal: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility; Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as flourishing.
units.idiomatic: Hence King Wen of Zhou with many scholars achieved tranquility, and Emperor Wu of Han took obtaining the worthy as his glory.

units.zh: 此載籍之所記，由來之常義。
units.literal: This the records memorialize—the constant meaning from antiquity.
units.idiomatic: Such is what the records memorialize—the constant meaning handed down from antiquity.

units.zh: 其餘亦用舊名不改。
units.literal: The rest likewise kept old names unchanged.
units.idiomatic: The remaining titles again stayed as they were.

units.zh: 及武帝受禪，乃令傅玄制為二十二篇，亦述以功德代魏。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu accepted abdication, he ordered Fu Xuan to compose twenty-two pieces, likewise narrating merit and virtue replacing Wei.
units.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the abdicated throne he told Fu Xuan to write twenty-two lyrics chronicling Jin merit supplanting Wei.

units.zh: 改《朱鷺》為《靈之祥》，言宣帝之佐魏，猶虞舜之事堯，既有石瑞之徵，又能用武以誅孟達之逆命也。
units.literal: They changed 《Red Egret》 to 《Auspice of the Numina》, referring to how Emperor Xuan aided Wei as Yu Shun served Yao, having both the omen of stone talisman and the ability to use arms to execute Meng Da's treasonous command.
units.idiomatic: 《Red Egret》 became 《Omen of the Spirits》, likening Sima Yi's service to Wei to Shun serving Yao: stone omens appeared and arms crushed Meng Da's revolt.

units.zh: 改《有所思》為《惟庸蜀》，言文帝既平萬乘之蜀，封建萬國，復五等之爵也。
units.literal: They changed 《I Had Someone in Mind》 to 《Only That Shu》, referring to how Emperor Wen pacified the Shu host of ten thousand chariots, enfeoffed myriad states, and restored the five grades of nobility.
units.idiomatic: 《I Had Someone in Mind》 became 《That Shu Alone》, for Sima Zhao's reduction of the Shu empire, investiture of countless domains, and revival of the five noble ranks.

units.zh: 改《芳樹》為《天序》，言聖皇應曆受禪，弘濟大化，用人各盡其才也。
units.literal: They changed 《Fragrant Trees》 to 《Heaven's Ordering》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the calendar and received abdication, broadly aided great transformation, and employed each man to his full talent.
units.idiomatic: 《Fragrant Trees》 turned into 《Heaven's Sequence》, celebrating the sage ruler's calendar-abdication, vast transformation, and each talent fully used.

units.zh: 改《上邪》為《大晉承運期》，言聖皇應籙受圖，化象神明也。
units.literal: They changed 《Oh Heaven Above》 to 《Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season》, referring to how the sage emperor answered the tallies and received the charts, transforming likeness spirit-like.
units.idiomatic: 《Oh Heaven Above》 became 《Great Jin's Hour》, because the sage sovereign answered the tally-charts and merged his likeness with the divine.

units.zh: 改《君馬黃》為《金靈運》，言聖皇踐阼，致敬宗廟，而孝道行於天下也。
units.literal: They changed 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 to 《The Metal Essence's Course》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne, paid utmost homage at the ancestral shrine, and filial devotion ran through the realm.
units.idiomatic: 《Your Horse Is Yellow》 was renamed 《Metal Virtue in Motion》, praising accession, ancestral devotion, and filial teaching across the land.

units.zh: 改《雉子班》為《于穆我皇》，言聖皇受禪，德合神明也。
units.literal: They changed 《Pheasant Broods》 to 《Oh Solemn Our Sovereign》, referring to how the sage emperor received abdication and virtue matched spirit luminaries.
units.idiomatic: 《Pheasant Broods》 became 《How Majestic Our King》, for the abdicated accession and virtue mirroring the gods.

units.zh: 改《聖人出》為《仲春振旅》，言大晉申文武之教，畋獵以時也。
units.literal: They changed 《The Sage Appears》 to 《Second Month Drills the Host》, referring to how Great Jin extended civil and martial teaching and hunted according to season.
units.idiomatic: 《The Sage Appears》 was titled 《Spring Hunt Drills the Troops》, recording Jin extension of civil-martial instruction and seasonal hunts.

units.zh: 改《石留》為《順天道》，言仲冬大閱，用武修文，大晉之德配天也。
units.literal: They changed 《Stone Stays》 to 《Obeying Heaven's Way》, referring to how in mid-winter the grand review used arms to cultivate culture, Great Jin's virtue matching heaven.
units.idiomatic: 《Stone Stays》 was renamed 《Following Heaven's Road》, for midwinter grand reviews where arms perfected culture and Jin matched heaven.

units.zh: 改《務成》為《唐堯》，言聖皇陟帝位，德化光四表也。
units.literal: They changed 《Accomplishing Completion》 to 《Tang Yao》, referring to how the sage emperor ascended the throne of emperor and moral transformation irradiated the four outer regions.
units.idiomatic: 《Accomplishing Completion》 became 《Emperor Yao of Tang》, because the sage ruler mounted the throne and edifying virtue lit the four quarters.

units.zh: 《玄雲》依舊名，言聖皇用人，各盡其材也。
units.literal: 《Dark Clouds》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor employed men, each to his material.
units.idiomatic: 《Dark Clouds》 stayed unchanged, depicting every talent placed according to his gifts.

units.zh: 改《黃爵行》為《伯益》，言赤烏銜書，有周以興，今聖皇受命，神雀來也。
units.literal: They changed 《Yellow Sparrow March》 to 《Boy Yi》, referring to how the red crow bore writing—Zhou rose thereby—and now the sage emperor received the mandate and spirit magpies came.
units.idiomatic: 《Yellow Sparrow March》 became 《Helper Yi》, comparing the crimson crow's writ that launched Zhou to the spirit finches greeting Jin's charge.

units.zh: 《釣竿》依舊名，言聖皇德配堯舜，又有呂望之佐，濟大功，致太平也。
units.literal: 《Fishing Rod》 kept its old name, referring to how the sage emperor's virtue matched Yao and Shun and he also had Lü Wang's assistance to accomplish great work and bring about great peace.
units.idiomatic: 《Fishing Rod》 remained, pairing Jin virtue with Yao-Shun and Lü Wang's aid to finish the great task of peace.

units.zh: 其辭並列之於後雲。
units.literal: Their lyrics are all listed below.
units.idiomatic: The texts follow in order.

title.zh: 卷二十八 志第十八 五行中
title.en: Volume 28 Treatises 18: Five Elements Part Two
title.raw: 卷二十八 志第十八 五行中 Volume 28 Treatises 18: Five Elements Part Two

units.zh: 劉毅上疏曰：「必有阿黨之臣奸以事君者，當誅而不赦也。」
units.literal: Liu Yi submitted a memorial saying: "There must be partisan ministers who deceive the ruler — they should be executed without pardon."
units.idiomatic: Liu Yi submitted a memorial saying: "There must be partisan ministers who deceive the ruler — they should be executed without pardon."

units.zh: 帝不答。
units.literal: The emperor did not answer.
units.idiomatic: The throne stayed silent.

units.zh: 是時荀勖、馮紞僭作威福，亂朝尤甚。
units.literal: At that time Xun Xu and Feng Dan presumptuously wielded favor and terror, disordering the court worst of all.
units.idiomatic: Xun Xu and Feng Dan terrorized the bureaucracy unchecked.

units.zh: 太熙元年二月，旱。
units.literal: Second month — drought.
units.idiomatic: Taixi 1's second month brought yet another dry spell.

units.zh: 自太康已後，雖正人滿朝，不被親仗，而賈充、荀勖、楊駿、馮紞等迭居要重，所以無年不旱者，欲德不用，上下皆蔽，庶位逾節之罰也。
units.literal: Since Taikang, although upright men filled the court they were not trusted; Jia Chong, Xun Xu, Yang Jun, Feng Dan and others rotated through critical posts — hence drought year after year: desired virtue unused, high and low blocked, common officers overstepping — their punishment.
units.idiomatic: The litany blames perennial drought on Sima Yan's trust in Jia, Xun, Yang, and Feng while excluding honest ministers.

units.zh: 惠帝元康七年七月，秦、雍二州大旱，疾疫，關中饑，米斛萬錢。
units.literal: Seventh month of Emperor Hui — great drought in Qin and Yong provinces, pestilence, Guanzhong famine, rice ten thousand cash per hu.
units.idiomatic: Yuankang 7's seventh month left Guanzhong buying grain at ten thousand cash a hu.

units.zh: 因此氐羌反叛，雍州刺史解系敗績。
units.literal: Thereupon Di and Qiang rebelled; Yongzhou inspector Jie Xi was defeated.
units.idiomatic: Di and Qiang uprisings followed, crushing Inspector Jie Xi.

units.zh: 是年春，三王討趙王倫，六旬之中數十戰，死者十餘萬人。
units.literal: That spring the three kings campaigned against Prince Zhao Lun; within sixty days dozens of battles, more than a hundred thousand dead.
units.idiomatic: The war on Sima Lun killed over a hundred thousand in two months.

units.zh: 懷帝永嘉三年五月，大旱，襄平縣梁水淡池竭，河、洛、江、漢皆可涉。
units.literal: Emperor Huai — fifth month great drought; Liang River's brackish pool in Xiangping dried; the Yellow, Luo, Yangzi, and Han could be waded.
units.idiomatic: Yongjia 3 shriveled rivers until fords appeared on the great streams.

units.zh: 是年三月，司馬越歸京都，遣兵入宮，收中書令繆播等九人殺之，皆僭逾之罰也。
units.literal: That year's third month Sima Yue returned to the capital, sent troops into the palace, seized Zhongshu Ling Miu Bo and nine others and killed them — all punishments for presumption.
units.idiomatic: Sima Yue's palace coup and execution of Miu Bo's circle exemplified overreach.

units.zh: 去歲十一月，司馬越以行台自隨，斥黜宮衛，無君臣之節。
units.literal: Eleventh month of last year Sima Yue brought his field headquarters along, cashiered palace guards — no ruler-subject propriety.
units.idiomatic: Sima Yue's mobile headquarters and dismissal of household guards broke every bond of ceremony.

units.zh: 元帝建武元年六月，揚州旱。
units.literal: Emperor Yuan — sixth month, Yang Province drought.
units.idiomatic: Jianwu 1's sixth month parched the lower Yangzi.

units.zh: 去年十二月，淳于伯冤死，其年即旱，而太興元年六月又旱。
units.literal: Last year's twelfth month Chunyu Bo died wrongfully; that year was drought, and Taixing 1 sixth month drought again.
units.idiomatic: The unjust execution of Chunyu Bo prefaced back-to-back drought years.

units.zh: 刑罰妄加，群陰不附，則陽氣勝之罰也。
units.literal: When punishments are wantonly applied and the many yin do not cleave, it is yang prevailing — punishment.
units.idiomatic: False justice, alienated ministers, and drought march together.

units.zh: 元帝太興四年五月，旱。
units.literal: Emperor Yuan — fifth month, drought.
units.idiomatic: Taixing 4's fifth month stayed dry.

units.zh: 是時王敦陵僭已著。
units.literal: At that time Wang Dun's arrogation was already plain.
units.idiomatic: Wang Dun's bullying had become unmistakable.

units.zh: 其閏十一月，京都大旱，川穀並竭。
units.literal: That intercalary eleventh month the capital great drought; rivers and valleys alike ran dry.
units.idiomatic: By leap-month winter even the capital's streams had failed.

units.zh: 明帝太寧三年，自春不雨，至於六月。
units.literal: Emperor Ming — from spring no rain until the sixth month.
units.idiomatic: Ming-di's Taining 3 saw not a shower from spring into summer.

units.zh: 成帝咸和元年，夏秋旱。
units.literal: Emperor Cheng — drought in summer and autumn.
units.idiomatic: Cheng-di's Xianhe opening scorched summer and fall.

units.zh: 是時庾太后臨朝稱制，言不從而僭逾之罰也。
units.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Yu held court and issued edicts — punishment for words unheeded and presumption.
units.idiomatic: Yu Wenjun's regency supplied the political gloss for the weather.

units.zh: 咸康元年六月，旱。
units.literal: Sixth month — drought.
units.idiomatic: Xiankang 1 opened with a June drought.

units.zh: 是時成帝沖弱，未親萬機，內外之政，決之將相。
units.literal: At that time Emperor Cheng was young and weak, had not yet taken the myriad threads; inner and outer policy was decided by generals and ministers.
units.idiomatic: The boy emperor left statecraft to generals and ministers.

units.zh: 此僭逾之罰，連歲旱也。
units.literal: This punishment for presumption — drought year after year.
units.idiomatic: Yearly drought was the fine for usurped authority.

units.zh: 時王導以天下新定，務在遵養，不任刑罰，遂盜賊公行，頻五年亢旱，亦舒綬之應也。
units.literal: At that time Wang Dao, because the realm was newly settled, aimed at nurturing and ease, would not employ punishments; thereupon bandits walked openly; five years running severe drought — also an omen of slack government.
units.idiomatic: Wang Dao's soft hand let robbers roam and drought linger five years — the price of lax rule.

units.zh: 康帝建元元年五月，旱。
units.literal: Emperor Kang — fifth month, drought.
units.idiomatic: Kang-di's the first year of Jianyuan fifth month added another dry entry.

units.zh: 穆帝永和元年五月，旱。
units.literal: Emperor Mu — fifth month, drought.
units.idiomatic: Yonghe 1's fifth month brought drought under Emperor Mu.

units.zh: 是時帝在襁褓，褚太后臨朝，如明穆太后故事。
units.literal: At that time the emperor was still in swaddling clothes; Empress Dowager Chu held court, following the precedent of Empress Dowager Mingmu.
units.idiomatic: The boy on the throne left regency to Empress Dowager Chu, as under Mingmu before.

units.zh: 永和五年七月不雨，至于十月。
units.literal: Fifth year, seventh month — no rain until the tenth month.
units.idiomatic: From midsummer through autumn Yonghe 5 stayed utterly dry.

units.zh: 升平四年冬，大旱。
units.literal: Fourth year, winter — great drought.
units.idiomatic: Shengping 4's winter repeated the calamity.

units.zh: 哀帝隆和元年夏，旱。
units.literal: Emperor Ai — summer, drought.
units.idiomatic: Longhe 1's summer parched the realm under Emperor Ai.

units.zh: 是時桓溫強恣，權制朝廷，僭逾之罰也。
units.literal: At that time Huan Wen acted with force and license, controlling the court at will — punishment for presumption.
units.idiomatic: Huan Wen's stranglehold on the court explained the omen.

units.zh: 涼州春旱至夏。
units.literal: Liangzhou — spring drought through summer.
units.idiomatic: The northwest baked from spring into summer.

units.zh: 簡文帝咸安元年十月，大旱，饑。
units.literal: Emperor Jianwen — tenth month, great drought, famine.
units.idiomatic: Xianan 1's tenth month brought famine-level drought.

units.zh: 自永和至是，嗣主幼沖，桓溫陵僭，用兵征伐，百姓怨苦。
units.literal: From Yonghe until then the successors were infants; Huan Wen bullied and usurped authority; armies marched; the people groaned.
units.idiomatic: Decades of child emperors and Huan Wen's wars had exhausted the country.

units.zh: 孝武帝甯康元年三月，旱。
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, Ningkang first year, third month — drought.
units.idiomatic: Ningkang 1 opened dry under Xiaowu.

units.zh: 是時桓溫入覲高平陵，闔朝致拜，逾僭之應也。
units.literal: At that time Huan Wen entered court for Gaoping Mausoleum; the whole court bowed to him — an omen of overstepping.
units.idiomatic: Huan Wen's reception at the mausoleum flouted every sumptuary rule.

title.zh: 卷15 志第10 音樂下
title.raw: 卷15 志第10 音樂下 Volume 15 Treatises 10: Music 3

units.zh: 又制樂舞，名曰《章斌》之舞，有事於天地宗廟及臨朝大饗，並用之。
units.literal: He also regulated a music-dance called the Zhang Bin dance, used together for rites to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples, and for grand feasts at court audiences.
units.idiomatic: He also instituted the Zhang Bin dance for Heaven-and-Earth and temple rites and for great court banquets.

units.zh: 晉武帝泰始二年，遣傅玄等造行禮及上壽食舉歌詩。
units.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, Fu Xuan and others were dispatched to compose songs for processional rites, longevity toasts, and banquet music.
units.idiomatic: In second year of Jin of Taishi, Fu Xuan and others were sent to write processional, longevity, and banquet songs.

units.zh: 張華表曰：「按漢、魏所用，雖詩章辭異，興廢隨時，至其韻逗曲折，並系於舊，一皆因襲，不敢有所改也。」
units.literal: Zhang Hua memorialized: "Examining what Han and Wei used, although the texts of the poems differ and pieces rose and fell with the times, their cadences and turns all depend on the old models—every one was inherited, and none dared to be altered."
units.idiomatic: Zhang Hua wrote: "Han and Wei pieces differ in wording and came and went with the times, but their phrasing and turns all followed old models—nothing was boldly changed."

title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

units.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
units.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.
units.idiomatic: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.

units.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
units.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.
units.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.

units.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
units.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;
units.idiomatic: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;

units.zh: 咸熙元年，追號宣穆妃。
units.literal: In the first Xianxi year she was posthumously titled Consort Xuanmu.
units.idiomatic: In 264 she received the posthumous title Consort Xuanmu.

units.zh: 及武帝受禪，追尊為皇后。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she was posthumously honored as empress.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, she was raised posthumously to empress.

units.zh: 景懷夏侯皇后
units.literal: Empress Xiahou Jinghuai
units.idiomatic: Empress Xiahou the Revered and Cherished

units.zh: 青龍二年，遂以鴆崩，時年二十四，葬峻平陵。
units.literal: In the second Qinglong year she then died by poisoned wine, aged twenty-four, buried at Junping tumulus.
units.idiomatic: In 234 she was poisoned at twenty-four and buried at Junping mausoleum.

units.zh: 武帝登阼，初未追崇，弘訓太后每以為言，泰始二年始加號諡。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, at first he did not posthumously honor her; Empress Dowager Hongxun often spoke of it; only in the second Taishi year did he begin adding title and posthumous name.
units.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne he left her unhonored until Empress Dowager Yang at Hongxun repeatedly pressed the matter; only in 266 did he grant posthumous rank and epithet.

units.zh: 后無男，生五女。
units.literal: The empress had no sons; she bore five daughters.
units.idiomatic: She had no sons but five daughters.

units.zh: 景懷皇后崩，景帝更娶鎮北將軍濮陽吳質女，見黜，復納后，無子。
units.literal: When Empress Jinghuai died, Emperor Jing further married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed; he then took in the empress; she had no sons.
units.idiomatic: After Empress Xiahou died, Emperor Jing married the daughter of Wu Zhi of Puyang, General Who Guards the North; she was dismissed, and he then married Yang Huiyu; she bore no sons.

units.zh: 武帝受禪，居弘訓宮，號弘訓太后。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, she resided in Hongxun Palace, titled Empress Dowager Hongxun.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu assumed the throne she moved to Hongxun Palace as dowager.

units.zh: 泰始九年，追贈蔡氏濟陽縣君，諡曰穆。
units.literal: In the ninth Taishi year Lady Cai was posthumously endowed as Mistress of Jiyang County, posthumous name Mu.
units.idiomatic: In 273 her mother was posthumously named Lady of Jiyang with the epithet Mu.
